drivers: Record copper output ~890K tonnes (2025) — strong export earnings
Record maize harvest >4M tonnes — reduced food import needs
Debt restructuring ~94% complete — sovereign risk premium collapsing
IMF ECF programme completed (final US$190M disbursement) — successor programme talks next
MPR held at 13.25% at the August 2026 MPC (26 Aug) — lowest since mid-2024; attractive real yields still support carry inflows
Yuan mining tax corridor reducing USD demand
Gross international reserves at historic high of US$5.5 billion
Swearing-in of President Hichilema and Vice-President for a second term held 1 Sep 2026 (public holiday) — policy continuity now formalised
BoZ cut statutory reserve requirements (early Aug 2026) — supportive of bank liquidity
Seasonal import demand and month-end FX demand pressuring the kwacha in mid-September
trendAnalysis.outlook: Kwacha softened ~0.85% to ~K19.40/USD mid on 17 Sep (open.er-api.com), giving back the prior session's gains as seasonal import and end-of-quarter FX demand returned, while remaining inside the broad 18.40–19.50 consolidation band. The move was broad-based: GBP, EUR, ZAR, BWP and CNY all edged higher against the kwacha. The official/parallel premium remains narrow (~+1.8%), signalling no acute FX scarcity. With re-election formalised at the 1 Sep ceremony and the MPC holding at 13.25% on 26 August, focus shifts to the 30 Sep MPC — the same day a 10% copper-concentrate export duty takes effect — plus the 2027 budget and the make-up of the new economic team.
trendAnalysis.projection3m: USD/ZMW 18.50–19.80 range. Post-election policy continuity supportive; import demand and copper-price swings the main risks.
trendAnalysis.projection6m: USD/ZMW 18.00–20.00 range. Direction hinges on fiscal continuity and copper earnings.

news.title: Atomic Eagle secures US$10.9 million to advance uranium projects in Zambia, Niger
news.summary: Atomic Eagle's largest shareholder, Menel Energy and Resources Limited, has committed about US$10.9 million to support the company's uranium projects in Zambia and Niger, underscoring renewed interest in Zambian energy minerals beyond copper.

news.title: Zambia leads with foresight in preparing for the 2026/2027 supersized El Niño
news.summary: Government has directed all Permanent Secretaries, Provincial Administrations and Local Authorities to activate contingency plans for the anticipated 2026/2027 supersized El Niño, which could stress rivers, hydropower generation and agriculture.

news.title: ZCCM-IH set to expand business portfolio, targets mining, energy
news.summary: ZCCM Investments Holdings expects to significantly increase its power and copper capacity over the next two years as it broadens its portfolio across mining and energy — a signal of the state investment arm's growing role in the copper and power build-out.

news.title: Zambia, UAE firm sign agreement to develop solar projects
news.summary: Zambia signed an agreement with a UAE firm to develop solar power projects, adding to a pipeline of renewable energy deals aimed at easing the country's electricity deficit and supporting mining growth.

news.title: Musokotwane's Day-One Message: Zambia Moves From Stabilisation to Growth
news.summary: Finance Minister Dr Situmbeko Musokotwane has directed the Ministry of Finance and National Planning to shift focus from macroeconomic stability toward investment, production, exports, jobs and higher incomes — formalising the "Grow Zambia" agenda.

news.title: Cabinet Sets 2027 Budget Priorities: Growth, Jobs and Tax Compliance
news.summary: Cabinet has set Zambia's 2027 budget priorities — jobs and human capital, stronger tax compliance and climate resilience — alongside continued deficit and debt reduction. The budget is due to be tabled in the Thirteenth Parliament.
